COAL THEFT 3.0

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Coal theft like you’ve never seen it before. We go undercover in the ultimate sting to catch the crooks – red handed.

Unique Selling Point:
- ONE OF CB's MOST ELABORATE STINGS EVER


Summary:
We know the drill - opportunistic criminals target transport company drivers to steal loads and loads of coal for a fee. We’ve shown how it happened after the fact, now we go undercover and show you first hand how it’s done.

But the real shock factor is that this sting is small fry. The real coal mafia is hard work as coal theft has evolved into a sophisticated criminal network – the modus operandi have morphed and we will be exposing a brand new one.


Further information:
TWO ELEMENTS TO THE STORY
1. THE STING - OLD ROGUE CAUGHT RED HANDED
2. COAL THEFT 3.0 - THE EVOLUTION OF COAL THEFT

UNDERSTANDING THE PROCESS
1. Transporters will be contracted to move tons of coal from a mine (POINT A) to a processing plant or power station or railway station for export (POINT B).
2. Collection slips are issued when the trucks are loaded at POINT A.
3. At POINT B – delivery notes are issued when the loads are dropped off.

THE THEFT - not all the loads make it from POINT A to POINT B. Some loads are stolen out right while others switched with a lesser grade of coal.
a. Drivers are approached by a middleman to drop the load off at another location along the route between A & B for a fee of R2500 – R12000.
b. Delivery notes are jippo-ed and the receiving company at POINT B is none the wiser of the loss.

THE STING
A Repeat Offender Clerrence Holtmann makes a second appearance. We have managed to secure a truck and a load of coal. We will send in an operative to sell this load to the one and only Clerrence Holtmann at a yard that is known for receiving stolen coal.

We build a scene around it – the set up beforehand, the return and then the confront.


COAL THEFT 3.0 THE EVOLUTION OF COAL THEFT
This time round criminal syndicates have streamlined their thieving operations.

THE NEW MO
1. A legitimate transporter has a contract from a mine to move coal from Point A to Point B. In this case from Belfast to Richardsbay for export.
2. This transporter is approached by a smaller transport company with 15 trucks asking for work – the transporter does due diligence, and appoints the smaller company as a sub-contractor.
3. The sub-contractor collects 50 loads from the mine, and gives the transporter that contracted them all the paper work stating the load were delivered – the stamped delivery notes, photos of the sealed loads – everything that’s required.

BUT ALL IS NOT AS IT SEEMS
The mine contacts the transporter – 50 loads were never received – the paper work was forged. No loads collected by the sub-contractor was EVER delivered. Those 50 loads were stolen.

THIS SUB-CONTRACTOR GOT THE JOB WITH THE SOLE PURPOSE OF STEALING!!!

HOW BIG IS THE PROBLEM?
This is not an isolated problem – coal theft plagues the industry across South Africa. The black market for coal is thriving because there is a huge demand for coal locally and for export. So if you can get a cheap load that you can sell at premium prices – dodgy dealers are willing to look the other way.

LOSSES
The stolen loads would have been paid for the company meant to receive the cargo because the paperwork in terms of the jippo-ed delivery notes will check out. But the dodgy dealers buying the stolen loads will then re-sell the cargo back into the market – essentially one loads would be paid for TWICE!

Because there are insiders involved, the paperwork checks out – but it is only when stock takes are done by the receiving companies that the losses are noted. For example, a company would have paid for 100 000 tones, but only received 80 000.

HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY?
- This will be a presenter driven investigation. Coal Theft is not new – we’ve shown you how it’s stolen, how it’s switched – but always after the fact – now we’ll show have it’s done in one of our most elaborate undercover stings yet!
- We connect with an informant – that reached out earlier this year – the same culprits we exposed last year were still at it. Months of investigations confirmed the allegations
- Interview Danie Day – he’s been on the trail before and still is – having tracked a stolen load just last month to the exact same yard we’ve been investigating.
- Then THE STING
- BUT it’s gotten much worse… there really is a COAL MAFIA at play – they are sophisticated in their schemes.
- A BIGGER PICTURE INDUSTRY EXPERT breaks it down.
- We have a case study of a recent group – COAL THEFT 3.0…
- AND THEN WE WRAP… WILL IT END…. WHO KNOWS…


INDUSTRY EXPERT – SCHALK DU PREEZ
Poerie van Rooyen heads up the coal theft investigations for a group of mines - he will explain the black market and how these syndicates have evolved their modus operandi’s incorporating tech and elaborate schemes to steal coal – it’s no longer the odd dodgy driver – it’s the coal mafia at work.

COAL THEFT 3.0 STRUCTURE

VO: Coal Theft… on our radar for years, we’ve exposed a number of criminal syndicates and their various Modus Operandi. Like all crimes, MOs evolve, so we’re infiltrating Mpumalanga’s illegal coal market, in our most complex sting to date.

AGENT: It’s a ghost load. // I need the money.

VO: It’s a lucrative illicit trade run by brazen rogues….

UNDERCOVER UPSOUNDS
WORKER 2: Do those camera’s work?
AGENT: Hai! //

VO: And, as we discover, some, are repeat offenders….

UPSOUND CLERRENCE: Don't speak sh** to me! You wish you got me.

VO: …and others, grow hostile at the threat of being exposed.

UPSOUND PRODUCER: Kom uit // loop vinnig //ons moet aan die ander kant van die hek kom - hier’s baie mense…

DRONE SHOT VAN KAR… 2-3 secondes…

LINK: Earlier this year we were contacted by a source in the coal industry. He says since our last exposé. Not only is the coal theft still happening, it's gotten worse, and it's apparently by the same people. He's agreed to speak to us if we protect his identity.

VO: There’s much at stake… the coal racket means big money.

GOVAN: Just tell me, why did you decide to contact Carte Blanche?
SOURCE: The information that I've got I think will definitely suit you. There is definitely stolen coal being handled in Middleburg, just outside Middleburg.
GOVAN: Is there demand for stolen coal?
SOURCE: Very much.

VISUAL BEAT - could be shorter

VO: To meet that demand, the criminals are determined to get their hands on coal ,by any means necessary. So they target transport company drivers willing to sell their cargo for a quick buck. With so many coal trucks around, there's no shortage of targets. And buyers, mostly dodgy coal yard owners, are ready, and waiting.

LINK: The profit margins are massive for the illegal coal yard owners. They buy the stolen coal at a fraction of the price and then sell it back at market value. And at the current rate, they're making a fortune.

VO: IN 2022 – we exposed how high-grade coal was being switched out for a lower quality product en route to its destination. Truck drivers were basically stealing the coal and selling it to dodgy coal yards.

UPSOUND COAL SWITCH 2022 -
MAC: Tell me Bra, Who’s on the owner here?

VO: At the time, we confronted this man: Clerrence Holtmann , a coal distributor operating a yard (HTH ) in Mpumalanga.

UPSOUND COAL SWITCH 2022
CLERRENCE: I am not even the one stealing coal.
MAC: Listen Clerrence… We're not making your name. The trucks came here. They switched coal. We've got the evidence, We've got the data, we've got the GPS locations. So don't tell us that we're making your name bad…

A BEAT BEFORE NEXT CLIP

SOURCE: The whole coal industry spoke about Clerrence Holtmann. He looks like an open, straightforward guy, but the, the intentions is not always there. He doesn't have a good name in the industry. He's still trying to defend himself, that there was no proof he was not arrested.

VO: Clerrence later contacted us, complaining about the impact of our expose.

CLERRENCE: I just want to know what's the procedure to clean my name. This Carte Blanche is killing me with this, that it's still on the internet and all of that stuff. It’s tough for me to do business like that.

VO: According to our source, Clerrence has been doing the same kind of business for years.

And it appears he may be right. Private Investigators Danie Day & Juan Burger, started looking into coal theft in 2019. Four years on, the same suspects keep cropping up.

JUAN: They're not going to stop. It's easy money and no one's knocking on the door to actually stop them.

VO: In November last year, Burger located a client’s truck at an unknown site after it deviated from its route. The coal yard in question is linked to Clerrence Holtmann and his partner , Steven Venter.

JUAN: If it wasn't for the tracking and the the footage from the drivercam, we obviously wouldn't have known that it was off loaded there.
FINAL MIX GOVAN RE-READ QUESTION
VO: Was this an illegal deal? [ORIGINAL This was clearly an illegal deal? ]
JUAN: Well, definitely the truck wasn't supposed to be there. The truck was supposed to be on en route to Richards Bay. / And the truck wasn't just empty. It was fully loaded with with Duff.//

VO: It was a typical coal switch case - the better quality coal was offloaded and replaced with a much cheaper, inferior product known, as Duff.

GOVAN: What did they say when you confronted them?
JUAN: They came up that they don't know why the truck would have entered the who would have opened. , they basically denied everything //. they didn't ask too many questions, just handed it back and arranged to have the load returned to the transport owner.

VO: But this wasn’t the only suspicious load tipped at this site. We know of at least two other transporters whose trucks were illegally offload here - one in June and another on August last year.

Clerrence Holtmann asked to meet us to - in his words - clear his name. We agreed .

GOVAN:We're just around the corner from Noodhulp, that’s Clerrence mine slash coal yard. It's where the drivers drop off the stolen coal.

VO: We’re holding back – while the investigators check if he’s around - we know from the last story, that Clerrence avoids cameras.

GOVAN: He's just not picking up the phone. // Security seems to be questioning him. They're coming to us now…
WIMPIE: I can’t hide the camera, dude.
GOVAN: Relax… [G covers up cam]

VO: Apparently he was at home, recovering from an injury.

GOVAN: There’s no doorbell… so we’ll have to call.

GOVAN: Can we talk? We heard you want to clear your name.
CLERRENCE: But you’re not going to show this ON TV and stuff, right? 00:03:28:13 - 00:03:33:14
GOVAN: We're from carte blanche, Clerrence. It's a TV show, you know that. 00:03:34:08 - 00:03:40:23 // Now it just looks like you're hiding. 00:04:38:19 - 00:04:44:06
CLERRENCE: JA, it's okay. 00:04:44:24 - 00:04:46:14 //
GOVAN: So listen, Clarence, I'll be straight with you. We know you're not doing legitimate business. 00:04:52:22 - 00:04:57:18
CLERRENCE: I have invoices and I have everything that I'm doing business legitimate, SO... 00:04:55:06
GOVAN: You're not doing that Clerrence.
CLERRENCE: I am!
GOVAN: They had to send a private investigator to recover stolen coal from your property. // 00:05:11:24 - 00:05:20:10
CLERRENCE: That was a truck wrongly in my yard.
GOVAN: It's happened three times already
CLERRENCE: No I don’t
GOVAN: in June, August and in November

VO: Clerrence refused an on-camera interview, but in later whatsapp messages stated they do legitimate business with mines and community groups, and have the paperwork to prove it.

He said: stealing three loads doesn’t make business sense as they mine and buy thousands of tons of coal a week. He denies any wrongdoing, saying they previously had unacceptable security on site, and now have new procedures in place.

But it’s not unusual for shady coal yard operators to deny wrongdoing and claim ignorance - even in an age of tracking data, tipper scale records and truck camera footage.

GOVAN: Do you think that the police are doing enough to curb coal theft?
JUAN: Not at all, if anything was done since 2019. The same syndicates won't be operating, As long as they're going to benefit financially from from this, they just going to keep going./ It's a ticking time bomb. It's just waiting to blow up.

VO: Amid the denials, claims, and counterclaims we decide to expose the culprits behind the theft of coal by setting up a sting operation.

We’re going to try and sell coal on the black market. To be clear, we’re not committing a crime: our coal isn’t really stolen - it’s our property and can be sold to anyone, at any price .

LINK: We’ve organised a truck, we’ve got a mine that’s going to give us coal, and everything is in place for our sting, now we’ll fill it up.

VO: The coal is known as RB2: it’s export quality, and selling a once off load should sound alarm bells for any legitimate trader.

A BEAT
UPSOUND CALL:
AGENT: Hi. Hello, boss. How are you?

VO: In this call, an undercover agentoffers the load to none other than Clerrence Holtmann.

UPSOUND CALL:
AGENT: I've got RB2. Can I come offload by you tomorrow?
CLERRENCE: JA.
AGENT: I need the money as soon as possible so that I can pay the guys that I'm working with. I've got four trucks that I can bring to you tomorrow.
CLERRENCE: It's fine.

VO: Take note, we offered to offload a specific grade of coal and asked about payment.
The deal is clear.

The truck is fully loaded and hidden cameras have been put in place.

GOVAN: Okay. Good luck. Good luck, my brother. All right. Thank you.

LINK: AllRight. The truck is off. This is the biggest sting that we've ever done. We've shown you stolen coal in the yard before. Now we'll show you how they buy it.

VO: Coming up in part 2.

VISUAL MOMENT
Worker - there is a load of Clerrence here.
UPSOUND GOVAN: No, I haven’t received the money yet Chief, when are you going to pay me?
GOVAN: Security with Knopkierries.


END PART ONE




 
PART TWO

VO: The black market for coal is a lucrative one - the profit margins are huge, the thieves are many and the coal traders are ready to buy.

In a major sting, we go undercover, infiltrating the illegal black market to see first hand how stolen coal is traded.

LINK: This is over 30 tons of coal. It's tens of thousands of rands. Everything has been set. We'll have our man on the inside

VO: A load of export grade RB2 coal, is worth about R65 000. In this case the coal isn’t actually stolen - it legally belongs to us. But the dodgy buyers don’t know that - and the origins of a single load like this, should be questioned.

But when we offered it to a coal trader, Clerrence Holtman, who we linked to stolen coal in our 2022 expose…. NO questions were asked.

En route, the undercover agentchecked in with Holtmann, confirming the drop off.

And it appeared, the guard, was expecting him.

GUARD: what do you have loaded?
NATHI: it’s RB2.
GUARD: For Clerrence
NATHI: yeh.

VO: On arrival, the agentswere asked to fill in a security register.

NATHI: is it necessary for us to fill in the form because we have a ghost load.
GUARD: hai, don’t worry.
NATHI: hmm is it not on the.
GUARD: hai this book is not given to anyone.
NATHI: hmm
GUARD: not even a high ranking policeman can touch it.

VO: Once inside the coal yard, he spoke to three more workers - explaining he was there to offload for Clerrence. No one asked for any documentation or proof of ownership. The only concern was the camera tech on the truck.

UNDERCOVER UPSOUNDS
WORKER 2: do those camera’s work?
NATHI: Hayi! Those cameras don't work and those things.It’s clean because it’s a ghost load.

VO: Clerrence’s partner, Steven Venter, was called about payment.

WORKER 2: There is a load of Clerrence here. It’s RB2, Ja, but he want the payment first
before he offloads.
STEVEN: Does he know how it works?
WORKER 2: After you offload, they pay you half and take a sample. Then they pay the balance.

VO: It’s clear that coal is there to be offloaded, the grade is mentioned and payment is discussed.

Steven Venter even made an appearance, and spoke to the operative.

UNDERCOVER CLIPS
STEVEN: What load is this?
NATHI: It’s RB2 - it’s coal
STEVEN: RB2?
NATHI: Yah
STEVEN It’s a load?
NATHI: JA, full load.
STEVEN: Let me find out what’s going on.

VO: But he just referred them back to Clerrence, who - remarkably - had a sudden change of story.

UPSOUND VOICE NOTE CLERRENCE:
Yeah, I misunderstood you,. I thought you want a load, a load of RB 2. I thought you want to buy. No my man we don't buy loads like this, huh.

VO: Our truck returned with the full load of coal…

GOVAN: Eish, my man. And then what happened?
NATHI: //We were shown to the right place , they didn't they didn't care whether I've got papers or not.
GOVAN: Knew that this was full of coal.
NATHI: Yeah, they knew // I think they were tipped off.
GOVAN: Neh
NATHI: I think they were tipped off.

VO: Despite the sale falling through, Clerrence has some explaining to do.

GOVAN: We know that you're almost you almost accepted coal in a sting operation. Then at the last moment, you pulled out
CLERRENCE: No I wouldn’t. Okay, it's fine. If you can just show me the proof.
GOVAN: We've got audio recordings // We've got all the proof.
CLERRENCE: You guys just f*** up people's lives with information that you get on the streets.
GOVAN: On the streets. Clerrence, it's your own voice. It's not on the streets. It's your own voice.
CLERRENCE: Don't speak sh** to me! //You wish you got me.

VO: Clerrence claims the agentwas selling cobbles - a product they buy from the local community. But that’s not true - the only product on offer was RB2 – export quality coal.

UPSOUND RB2 // RB 2 // RB 2

VO: There was no confusion about the quality of the product on offer. Clerrence’s reason for backing out, didn’t add up.

He continued to claim innocence as did his partner, Steven Venter. In a lawyer’s letter he said they run an entirely legitimate large coal business and that when difficulties arise they are dealt with accordingly. The security contractor had been changed and they continually inspect the yard in case any unauthorized vehicles are on the premises.

BEAT

VO: With that sale falling through - our sting hung in the balance. But after four years investigating coal country, we know, that where one coal yard won’t buy, another surely will.

SCHALK: Wherever there is coal, you'll find coal theft occurring

VO: Mining Security consultant, Schalk du Preez says the losses to the mining industry are crippling.

SCHALK: Intelligence sources and investigations are indicating that specific plots dealing in stolen coal will receive between 20 to 60 trucks per day.
GOVAN: Per day.
SCHALK: I mean, that is just that's one yard.

VO: Since 2019, at least 67 illegal operations have been identified in the area.

SCHALK: It looks like where we are standing now // It will have stockpiles. Some of these illegal traders have their own crushers,// Some of them. You know, if you look at their background, it's a legitimate registered company and you will deal in both legal and illegal coal.

VO: And with high local and international demand for coal, there’s no shortage of shady suppliers hunting for opportunity.

ADD A BEAT OR TWO BEFORE THE LINK

LINK: Selling the coal is as not as easy as it looks, //

UPSOUNDS CALLS -
KEEP GOVAN - Ok give him a call…
KEEP BUYER: I don’t need product now, I’m not buying any product now….
KEEP WELCOME TO VOICE MAIL


LINK: … these guys are cagey, it’s a big money business, so you need an in to get the deal done.

VO: We were stuck with a truck full of coal and no sign of a buyer..

NIGHT TIME WAITING \ hazards on…

VO: It took three days to eventually connect with a middleman and a buyer called Ibrahim - operating from a coal yard in Rondebult, Witbank.

He’s told it’s stolen coal on offer.

MIDDLEMAN: If you bring those trucks, I’ll pay you for one load.

VO: The drop was done in the early hours of the morning, using the darkness as cover.

RECEIVER: Yah, you must put it, there must be some space between them so that they don’t mix.

VO: We were promised an electronic payment by later that morning.

UPSOUND MIDDLEMAN: Just give me 30 minutes, then I will sort you, I’ll sort you out.

VO: With no payment by the afternoon, we went to the yard.

GOVAN…. There’s the piles of coal….you see them? At the back there…

GOVAN:This is the coal yard in a Rondebult. This place was flagged by Schalk. It's also the place that bought the stolen coal. Let's go try and find the buyer…. there it is.

GOVAN: Ek se Boeta – howzit, I'm looking Ibrahim.
WORKER: Ibrahim is not here…
GOVAN: We Want to speak to him about the coal that we dropped off here.
WORKER: you dropped off here?
GOVAN Yeah. This morning at around 2:00.

VO: It seems we know more than the workers….All that’s left is to contact the buyer directly.

With the deal still in play, I’m calling him posing as the seller of the dodgy coal.

GOVAN: No, I haven’t received the money yet Chief, when are you going to pay me?
IBRAHIM: You gonna get it man….
GOVAN: How long am I going to wait, Ibrahim?
IBRAHIM: Let me just make a call. I’ll call you back now…
GOVAN: Ok, it’s fine my brother, Sharp
IBRAHIM: Okay, shap-shap.
GOVAN: Confirms he bought the stolen coal, delaying us for the money. That's the nature of this business. They don't only scam the mines and the transporters, they scam each other. What he doesn't know is that it's a sting.

VO: Within minutes of making the call, the yard’s security crew showed up… so we moved off site.

GOVAN: Security with knopkierries.

VO: It looked like our sting was up, but the next day… payment was made.

PING….

VO: Ibrahim, though, had disappeared.

UPSOUND: Welcome to Voice Mail.

VO: If our sting demonstrates one thing, it’s that ridding the country of black market coal will require staying one step ahead of criminal syndicates with ever-evolving MOs. And as they continue evading the law, the cost to the country in lost revenue and load shedding, mounts.



END PART TWO

This transporter is approached by a smaller transport company with 15 trucks asking for work – the transporter does due diligence, and appoints the smaller company as a sub-contractor. 3. The sub-contractor collects 50 loads from the mine, and gives the transporter that contracted them all the paper work stating the load were delivered – the stamped delivery notes, photos of the sealed loads – everything that’s required. BUT ALL IS NOT AS IT SEEMS The mine contacts the transporter – 50 loads were never received – the paper work was forged. No loads collected by the sub-contractor was EVER delivered. Those 50 loads were stolen. THIS SUB-CONTRACTOR GOT THE JOB WITH THE SOLE PURPOSE OF STEALING!!! HOW BIG IS THE PROBLEM? This is not an isolated problem – coal theft plagues the industry across South Africa. The black market for coal is thriving because there is a huge demand for coal locally and for export. So if you can get a cheap load that you can sell at premium prices – dodgy dealers are willing to look the other way. LOSSES The stolen loads would have been paid for the company meant to receive the cargo because the paperwork in terms of the jippo-ed delivery notes will check out. But the dodgy dealers buying the stolen loads will then re-sell the cargo back into the market – essentially one loads would be paid for TWICE! Because there are insiders involved, the paperwork checks out – but it is only when stock takes are done by the receiving companies that the losses are noted. For example, a company would have paid for 100 000 tones, but only received 80 000. HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY? - This will be a presenter driven investigation. Coal Theft is not new – we’ve shown you how it’s stolen, how it’s switched – but always after the fact – now we’ll show have it’s done in one of our most elaborate undercover stings yet! - We connect with an informant – that reached out earlier this year – the same culprits we exposed last year were still at it. Months of investigations confirmed the allegations - Interview Danie Day – he’s been on the trail before and still is – having tracked a stolen load just last month to the exact same yard we’ve been investigating. - Then THE STING - BUT it’s gotten much worse… there really is a COAL MAFIA at play – they are sophisticated in their schemes. - A BIGGER PICTURE INDUSTRY EXPERT breaks it down. - We have a case study of a recent group – COAL THEFT 3.0… - AND THEN WE WRAP… WILL IT END…. WHO KNOWS… INDUSTRY EXPERT – SCHALK DU PREEZ Poerie van Rooyen heads up the coal theft investigations for a group of mines - he will explain the black market and how these syndicates have evolved their modus operandi’s incorporating tech and elaborate schemes to steal coal – it’s no longer the odd dodgy driver – it’s the coal mafia at work.
